photos.question: Which serum digoxin level is within the usual therapeutic range?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #378!

💓 Do you know the safe zone for this classic heart drug?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — 1.2 ng/mL

🧠 Rationale: The usual therapeutic digoxin level is about 0.5 to 2 ng/mL.

Levels above 2 ng/mL raise the risk of toxicity.

Low potassium makes toxicity more likely, even at normal levels.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Digoxin

💊 Drug Class:

🔹 Cardiac glycoside

❤️ Primary Use:

🔹 Heart failure

🔹 Atrial fibrillation rate control

⚠️ Signs of Toxicity:

🔹 Nausea, vomiting, poor appetite

🔹 Yellow or green halos in vision

🔹 Bradycardia and new dysrhythmias

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Count the apical pulse for 1 full minute

✅ Hold if adult HR is under 60 and notify provider

✅ Check potassium and digoxin levels

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Dig level 0.5 to 2: stay in the middle, watch the K!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Pharmacology #Cardiac #Digoxin #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A client takes tacrolimus after a kidney transplant. Which instruction is most important?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #379!

🫘 A new kidney needs this drug for life. What matters most?

This is a HIGH-YIELD renal and pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — Report fever or signs of infection

🧠 Rationale: Tacrolimus suppresses the immune system to prevent rejection.

This makes infections more likely and harder to spot.

Fever can be an early sign of infection or rejection.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Tacrolimus

💊 Drug Class:

🔹 Calcineurin inhibitor (immunosuppressant)

❤️ Primary Use:

🔹 Prevent organ transplant rejection

⚠️ Side Effects:

🔹 Infection risk

🔹 Kidney toxicity

🔹 High potassium and high blood glucose

🔹 Tremor

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Take at the same times every day

✅ Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice

✅ Never stop or skip doses on your own

✅ Report fever, chills, sore throat

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Immunosuppressed = infection risk. Fever is a red flag!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Renal #Transplant #Pharmacology #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A client just had a thoracentesis. Which finding should the nurse report right away?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #380!

🫁 The procedure went fine, but now one finding is a big warning sign. Can you spot it?

This is a HIGH-YIELD respiratory question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Sudden dyspnea and a fast heart rate

🧠 Rationale: A thoracentesis uses a needle to drain fluid from the pleural space.

The needle can puncture the lung and cause a pneumothorax.

Sudden dyspnea and tachycardia need immediate reporting.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Thoracentesis

🩺 Before:

🔹 Verify consent

🔹 Sit upright, leaning over a bedside table

⚠️ Watch For After:

🔹 Sudden shortness of breath

🔹 Falling SpO2, fast heart rate

🔹 Decreased breath sounds on that side

🔹 Bleeding at the site

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Check vital signs and SpO2 often

✅ Listen to breath sounds

✅ Expect a chest x-ray after

✅ Apply a dressing to the site

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Needle in the chest, new dyspnea next? Think pneumothorax!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Respiratory #Thoracentesis #Pneumothorax #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A client's ankle-brachial index (ABI) is 0.6. What does this result suggest?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #381!

🦵 One number tells you a lot about blood flow to the legs. Do you know what it means?

This is a HIGH-YIELD cardiovascular question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Peripheral arterial disease

🧠 Rationale: ABI compares ankle systolic BP to arm systolic BP.

A normal ABI is about 1.0 to 1.4.

Under 0.9 suggests peripheral arterial disease. 0.6 is moderate disease.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Ankle-Brachial Index

📏 How It Works:

🔹 Ankle systolic BP divided by arm systolic BP

⚠️ PAD Signs:

🔹 Leg pain with walking (claudication)

🔹 Cool, pale legs, weak pulses

🔹 Shiny, hairless skin

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Teach walking exercise programs

✅ Teach smoking cessation

✅ Keep legs level or slightly down for comfort

✅ Report sudden pain, pallor or no pulse

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

ABI under 0.9? The arteries are in trouble!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Cardiac #PAD #Vascular #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A client with acute pancreatitis has bluish bruising around the umbilicus. What does this suggest?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #382!

🔵 This bruise is a serious warning sign in pancreatitis. Do you know why?

This is a HIGH-YIELD GI question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Bleeding into the abdomen

🧠 Rationale: Bluish bruising around the umbilicus is Cullen sign.

In acute pancreatitis it suggests internal (retroperitoneal) bleeding.

Report it right away and watch closely for shock.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Acute Pancreatitis

⚠️ Key Signs:

🔹 Severe upper abdominal pain to the back

🔹 High serum lipase and amylase

🔹 Cullen sign: bruising around umbilicus

🔹 Grey Turner sign: bruising on the flanks

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Keep NPO to rest the pancreas

✅ Give IV fluids and pain medicine

✅ Watch BP and heart rate for shock

✅ Monitor calcium and glucose

🚑 When to Escalate:

🔹 Falling BP, rising heart rate

🔹 New bruising, confusion or low urine output

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Cullen = Center (umbilicus). Grey Turner = Turn to the flanks!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #GI #Pancreatitis #MedSurg #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: Two nurses are giving CPR to an infant. Which compression to breath ratio is correct?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #383!

👶 Two rescuers, one tiny patient. Do you know the right ratio?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pediatric question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — 15 compressions to 2 breaths

🧠 Rationale: With two rescuers, infant and child CPR uses 15:2.

A single rescuer uses 30:2.

Children need more breaths because arrest is often respiratory.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Infant CPR

🫀 Compressions:

🔹 Rate 100 to 120 per minute

🔹 Depth about 1.5 inches (4 cm)

🔹 Allow full chest recoil

👐 Hand Position:

🔹 2 thumb-encircling hands technique

🔹 Heel of one hand if you cannot encircle

🚨 Key Points:

✅ Check brachial pulse

✅ Minimize pauses in compressions

✅ Switch compressor about every 2 minutes

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Two rescuers, two hands, 15:2 for little ones!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: The nurse strokes the sole of an adult's foot. The big toe goes up and the toes fan out. What does this suggest?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #384!

🦶 Normal in a baby, a red flag in an adult. Do you know this reflex?

This is a HIGH-YIELD neuro question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — An upper motor neuron problem

🧠 Rationale: The big toe going up with toes fanning is a positive Babinski sign.

In adults it suggests an upper motor neuron problem.

In infants up to about 1 to 2 years it is normal.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Babinski Reflex

🩺 How to Test:

🔹 Stroke the outer sole from heel to toes

✅ Normal Adult:

🔹 Toes curl downward (plantar flexion)

⚠️ Abnormal Adult:

🔹 Big toe up, toes fan out

🔹 Seen with stroke, spinal cord injury, MS

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Document and compare both sides

✅ Report new findings to the provider

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Babies Babinski, adults alarm!
